entry_semantics.statement: rev: a 40-hex lane commit, or REV (the checker's --rev, for a corrected statement whose commit does not exist yet); path: lane-relative; line_regex: exactly one line of `git show rev:path` (split on \n, numbered like grep -n) matches, and its required (?P<stated>...) group quotes the stated number (digits or an English number word)
entry_semantics.stated: the integer the statement asserts; must equal the (?P<stated>...) text
entry_semantics.derive: argv: `python3 -I .ufo/waves/round-20/tally-check.py <receipt-files|pointer-token|selftest-labels> ...` only, every --rev/--counter-rev/--old/--new value 40-hex or REV, no --path/--counter value equal to the statement file, a --token value present in the statement line; run with cwd = lane over committed bytes only. extract_regex: begins (?m)^<count key>= with a key the subcommand declares, matches stdout exactly once; group 1 (or (?P<derived>...)) is the derived integer. A literal denominator such as /13 in both regexes binds the fraction's denominator.
entry_semantics.note: what is counted, how, and the measured value

set_semantics.red: stale round-19 statements read at their own pinned revision: each must print MISMATCH (`--set red` exits 1; `--set red --expect` exits 0 only when every red mismatches)
set_semantics.green: corrected statements (L1 adds them, usually at REV): each must print MATCH (`--set green --rev <commit>` exits 0); an empty set exits 2, never a vacuous pass
